P2: A configured `X-Environment-Key` in `custom_headers` replaces `config.environment_key`, sending API requests under the wrong environment. Reapply the SDK-owned environment key after merging custom headers.
Prompt for AI agents ```text Check if this issue is valid — if so, understand the root cause and fix it. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. At lib/flagsmith/sdk/api_client.rb, line 35: A configured `X-Environment-Key` in `custom_headers` replaces `config.environment_key`, sending API requests under the wrong environment. Reapply the SDK-owned environment key after merging custom headers. @@ -32,7 +32,7 @@ def build_headers(faraday, config) faraday.headers['X-Environment-Key'] = config.environment_key faraday.headers['User-Agent'] = Flagsmith::SDK::Utils.user_agent - faraday.headers.merge(config.custom_headers) + faraday.headers.merge!(config.custom_headers) end ```
```suggestion faraday.headers.merge!(config.custom_headers) faraday.headers['X-Environment-Key'] = config.environment_key ```

** Major** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win** **Keep custom credentials out of request logs.** With the default logger, a request now logs the configured `Authorization` and `X-Proxy-Token` values to stdout. Faraday 2.0.1 logs request headers at info level by default, and this client installs that logger without filters. Disable request-header logging or redact sensitive values while still sending them in requests. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith-ruby-client/f0033bd0b28b86f9cd2685b1a62bf891df023e97/lib/flagsmith/sdk/config.rb)) --- ** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Apply one precedence rule to `X-Environment-Key` in both clients.** `ApiClient#build_headers` sets `X-Environment-Key` to `config.environment_key`, then `merge!(config.custom_headers)` replaces it with any custom value. `EventProcessor#headers` gives the environment key precedence over custom headers. If `custom_headers` sets a different `X-Environment-Key`, flag requests and event requests can target different environments, and events can be attributed to the wrong environment. Choose one rule for conflicting `X-Environment-Key` values, and apply it in both `lib/flagsmith/sdk/api_client.rb` and `lib/flagsmith/sdk/event_processor.rb`. The current code uses opposite precedence in each client.

comments.body:
Walkthrough

`ApiClient#build_headers` now uses `merge!` to add configured custom headers to Faraday’s headers. A spec checks that the configured `Authorization` and `X-Proxy-Token` headers are present alongside the default `X-Environment-Key`. **Estimated code review effort:** 1 (Trivial) | ~5 minutes
Merge Risk: Moderate · up to f0033

The change makes configured custom headers reach API requests, as intended. With the default logger, those headers, including credentials, will now also appear in stdout logs. A conflicting environment-key header can also make flag and event requests use different environments. Address the logging exposure before merging, and decide on a single precedence rule for the environment key.
